correctness.rationale: The given expected-payoff death–birth model has u=-cx+bPx, positive fitness exp(delta[u_i+lambda_i(Pu)_i]), and uniform death with proportional-neighbor reproduction. Equality of all individual replacement probabilities at each vacancy is precisely equality of lambda_i(Pu)_i for each pair of common-neighbor competitors (relative fitness ratios). Fully cooperative configuration x=1 and variable b!=c forces lambda_i=lambda_k on each common-neighbor pair. Varying c while using binary basis configurations forces P_i=P_k whenever their shared lambda is nonzero. The common-neighbor auxiliary graph is connected for connected nonbipartite G, has exactly the two bipartition parts as components for connected bipartite G. No adjacent vertices can have equal loopless stochastic rows; any nonzero invisible profile thus forces G complete bipartite. Conversely on K_{a,b} identical P rows within each side imply sidewise constant lambda cancels out of all competing fitness ratios. Includes stars and K1,1, all delta>0, b,c>0, all binary states, arbitrary real part constants; same entire transition kernel follows. Independently enumerated 771 connected labeled loopless graphs of orders 2..5 and all {-1,0,1}^V profiles and verified exact equivalence; source P4 strategy witness gives competitor log-fitness difference delta/4. The unrestricted theorem relies on analytic common-neighbor proof, not finite testing.

value.rationale: Identifying every graph and nonzero susceptibility profile for which a seemingly nonlinear social-comparison perturbation leaves the entire microscopic Markov chain unchanged is a substantive structural invariance/boundary theorem. It distinguishes exact kernel invisibility for every positive selection strength from agreement of one weak-selection threshold, with direct consequences for parameter identifiability and games on stars/complete bipartite networks.

limitations: Strict δ>0, finite connected undirected loopless unweighted graphs, expected-payoff, all binary x and positive b,c; no result about weaker aggregated-state or fixation-only invariance.
